mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.5% compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as investors shift to risk assets during accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 4.5% but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods with this condition.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point monthly increase in unemployment rate signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 1 month but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in federal funds rate and core inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates effective monetary policy easing, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days through reduced real interest rates.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL declines in same month but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer spending (RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly) during early economic expansion phases drives positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days as corporate earnings gain momentum.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth > 0.5% and GDPC1 growth > 1.0% but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0 index) signals manufacturing contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as economic activity weakens.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100.0 but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point monthly decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) indicates labor market tightness, generating positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days via earnings growth expectations.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls < 3.5% in 1 month but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1,400.0 thousand units signals robust consumer demand for durable goods, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days as housing sector strength boosts economic confidence.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1400.0 but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of months.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY) combined with federal funds rate above 5.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days through reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 5.0% but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods.
